channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Ex-deputado George Santos é investigado por fraude em apostas nos EUA
item.description: Former U.S. congressman George Santos, of Brazilian descent, is under investigation by the U.S. Department of Justice for suspected fraud in prediction markets on the platform Kalshi, after betting against his own attendance at President Donald Trump’s State of the Union address despite publicly stating he would attend. Kalshi flagged suspicious trading activity before the event, when Santos’ attendance odds were near 75%, and he later claimed to have been detained at the airport minutes after the speech began. Santos was previously convicted in 2024 of fraud and identity theft, serving only 84 days before receiving a presidential pardon from Trump.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula promove reunião ministerial
item.description: President Lula chaired the second ministerial meeting of the year on June 3, 2026, to coordinate the government's response to escalating trade and security tensions with the United States. The meeting followed new U.S. tariff threats, including a proposed 25% duty on Brazilian goods over unfair trade practices and a 12.5% rate linked to forced labor, alongside the designation of PCC and CV as foreign terrorist organizations. The gathering aimed to align ministerial messaging amid the most strained bilateral relations in recent years.

item.title: Charge do JCaesar: 3 de junho
item.description: JCaesar's June 3, 2026 cartoon satirizes the relationship between Donald Trump and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, using commercial tariffs as the backdrop for political humor. The image likely critiques trade tensions between the U.S. and Brazil, portraying Trump as aggressive in his tariff policies and Lula as a figure attempting to navigate or respond to these pressures.

item.title: Lula faz reunião ministerial para alinhar governo antes da campanha e discutir tensão com os EUA
item.description: President Lula convenes his ministers at the Planalto Palace to align the government ahead of the 2026 elections and amid escalating trade tensions with the United States, following a U.S. recommendation for 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods. The meeting aims to unify messaging on government achievements and the response to U.S. measures, which the Planalto attributes to the Bolsonaro family's actions.

item.title: Tarifas dos EUA colocam comércio exterior e eleições na mesma arena
item.description: The USTR proposed 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, with exceptions for strategic sectors like beef, linking trade policy to the 2026 electoral landscape. The measure intensifies pressure on candidates to debate foreign policy and its economic impact on Brazil.

item.title: Análise: conta de tarifaço 2.0 está na mesa do bolsonarismo
item.description: The new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazil, dubbed 'tariff hike 2.0', has entered the 2026 pre-campaign as a central issue, with Lula and right-wing pre-candidates debating who will bear the cost. The measure is seen as a repeat of earlier episodes tied to Bolsonarist allies’ lobbying in the U.S., particularly Flávio Bolsonaro’s trip aiming to gain political capital by designating criminal factions as terrorist groups, which instead linked him to the tariff. Despite attempts to distance, political responsibility falls on the Bolsonarist camp.

item.title: O petista que cunhou o apelido 'Tariflávio'
item.description: The PT launched the nickname 'Tariflávio' for Flávio Bolsonaro, linking him to a proposed 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods. The initiative was shared on the party’s social media platforms yesterday morning as part of a political communication strategy. The full article is available only to subscribers.

item.title: Governo Lula já esperava novas sanções dos EUA por trabalho forçado e vai insistir no discurso eleitoral de soberania nacional
item.description: The Lula government anticipated new U.S. sanctions over alleged forced labor and will maintain a national sovereignty discourse in its official responses. The proposed tariffs are 12.5% on Brazilian products, part of a Section 301 investigation that also targets 59 other countries. The U.S. strategy aims to rebuild trade barriers on a stronger legal footing after a Supreme Court defeat.

item.title: De aborto à maioridade penal, oposição no Congresso tenta aprovar propostas que são bandeiras eleitorais antes da campanha
item.description: Opposition lawmakers are advancing right-wing electoral proposals ahead of the 2026 elections, including lowering the age of criminal responsibility to 14, loosening gun ownership requirements, and restricting legal abortion for minors under 14. These initiatives are tied to the pre-campaign of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), who has endorsed reducing the age of criminal responsibility as a response to juvenile crime. The bill restricting abortion for children has already been approved by the Senate and will take effect, while other measures remain under congressional review.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro abusam da retórica e fazem comédia de erros
item.description: Lula accused Flávio Bolsonaro and his family of being 'traitors of the homeland' for allegedly seeking foreign intervention in Brazilian affairs, comparing them to historical traitor Joaquim Silvério dos Reis. Flávio Bolsonaro countered by claiming Lula was encouraging criminal factions to kill him and threatened to take the matter to the STF, alleging the president wanted him hanged like Tiradentes. The exchange of harsh rhetoric raised concerns that the campaign is devolving into a 'comedy of errors'.

item.title: Fim da escala 6x1 sai antes da eleição? As pressões a favor e contra na reta final no Congresso
item.description: The proposal to end the 6x1 work scale was approved in the Chamber of Deputies, but its progress in the Senate remains uncertain due to President Davi Alcolumbre's cautious stance, advocating for calm debate and committee analysis before plenary vote. Meanwhile, 41 opposition senators, including pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, introduced an alternative PEC preserving the current work schedule and offering a flexible hours-based regime, without reducing weekly hours or guaranteeing two days off per week.

item.title: Viana, Cameli e Bittar empatam por vagas ao Senado no AC
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on June 3, 2026 shows a technical tie between Jorge Viana (PT), Gladson Cameli (PP) and Márcio Bittar (PL) in the race for Senate seats in Acre, with a 3.2-point margin of error. The study, registered with the TSE under AC-01182/2026, interviewed 1,000 people from May 31 to June 2, 2026, at a cost of R$40,000 funded by own resources. Since each state elects two senators in 2026, the total percentages do not sum to 100%.

item.title: Tiro ao Pix pode ser fatal para Flávio
item.description: The United States' threat to limit or embargo the use of Pix through tariffs or sanctions could significantly influence Brazil's 2026 elections, particularly if framed as an attack on national sovereignty. For Flávio Bolsonaro, running for Senate or another office, this issue could become a critical vulnerability, given his base's sensitivity to technological autonomy and resistance to foreign interference. The article suggests that if effectively amplified by opponents, such measures could undermine his credibility and popular support.

item.title: O novo tarifaço de Trump contra o Brasil - O Assunto #1733
item.description: The U.S. Trade Office concluded an investigation and proposed 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing unfair practices including Pix usage, illegal deforestation, piracy, and weak anti-corruption enforcement. The move sparked political reactions in Brazil, with Lula linking the tariffs to Bolsonaro’s family and the opposition coining the term 'tariflávio'. Although strategic goods like meat and aircraft are excluded, analysts see the tariff as having potential electoral impact in Brazil’s 2026 race.

item.title: Renan Santos diz que Trump beneficia Lula e Bolsonaro com ações
item.description: Renan Santos, a pre-candidate for Presidency, claimed that Donald Trump's actions benefit both Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, suggesting the proposed U.S. tariffs on Brazilian exports are part of a 'geopolitical game' that strengthens Lula by fueling a narrative of national defense. He noted that a similar situation occurred in 2025, when Flávio was seen by the opposition as a negotiator in bilateral talks.

item.title: Política é o tema mais associado a fake news no Brasil, aponta pesquisa
item.description: A study by Aláfia Lab shows that politics and elections are the topics most associated with the spread of fake news in Brazil, with 43% of Brazilians saying they encounter more false news on this subject than any other. The study reveals differences in perception and behavior between left, right, and center voters: while most claim to be able to identify misinformation (58% with doubts, 29% easily), groups like men, youth, and the more educated feel more confident, whereas right-wing voters report greater exposure to political fake news (55%) despite using fact-checking tools less (13%) compared to left-wing voters (24%).

item.title: Lula reúne ministros nesta quarta em meio a ofensivas dos EUA contra o Brasil
item.description: President Lula held a ministerial meeting on Wednesday (3) to address U.S. trade offensives, including a proposed 25% tariff on Brazilian goods and the designation of criminal factions as foreign terrorist organizations. This marks the first collective ministerial meeting since the April reshufflings, with expectations that issues such as the 6x1 workday and Jorge Messias’ STF nomination will be discussed in the context of the 2026 electoral debate.

item.title: Flávio diz, sem provas, que Lula incentivou facções a matá-lo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) accused President Lula of indirectly encouraging criminal factions like the PCC and Comando Vermelho to kill him, using the phrase 'dog whistle' to suggest a covert signal. The claim followed Lula's remark that Bolsonaro’s sons deserved the same fate as Tiradente for seeking U.S. support, which led to a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods. Flávio said he would file a complaint with the STF for threats and incitement to crime, despite historically misstating that Joaquim Silvério dos Reis was executed — when in fact he died of natural causes.

item.title: Lula critica Trump e Flávio, mas não prioriza o Pix ao cortar verba do BC
item.description: President Lula criticized Donald Trump's proposed tariffs and Flávio Bolsonaro's actions, but did not prioritize defending Pix when approving budget cuts to the Central Bank. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) was linked to a scenario that could enable attacks on Pix, though he made no direct statements against the system. The text highlights the tension between foreign policy, internal pressures, and the vulnerability of digital social programs amid budgetary decisions.

item.title: O movimento de Flávio Bolsonaro para recuperar espaço em reduto de Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is advancing his political agenda in the Northeast to recover lost ground after his recent absence from the region, particularly following controversies linked to his ties with banker Daniel Vorcaro and a meeting with Donald Trump in the U.S. His team has revised its initial plan to resume activities only during the São João festivities and now aims for a visit to Bahia on the 9th, pending logistical adjustments, to reconnect with northeastern voters and strengthen local alliances. The move also seeks to influence Bahia’s political landscape by boosting support for ACM Neto, the União Brasil gubernatorial candidate backed by the PL, who remains strategically neutral among center-right forces.

item.title: Zema e Caiado responsabilizam política externa de Lula por tarifaço
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) blamed Lula’s foreign policy for the proposed 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing lost credibility and legal security. They criticized the PT’s alleged alliances with dictators and supported the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist groups, while avoiding mention of Flávio Bolsonaro regarding tariffs. Both hinted at a potential alliance for the 2026 runoff against the PT, though their teams deny any formal agreement.

item.title: Flávio vai acionar STF contra Lula por incitação ao crime
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) announced he will file a complaint with the Supreme Federal Court against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) for alleged crimes of threat and incitement to violence, following Lula’s remarks calling the Bolsonaro family 'traitors' and likening them to Joaquim Silvério dos Reis during an event in Goiás. The lawsuit stems from Lula’s statements linking the Bolsonaro family to the proposed U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods and suggesting Flávio sought foreign intervention against him.

item.title: Renan Santos comemora R$ 500 mil em doação eleitoral
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential pre-candidate for the Missão party, celebrated surpassing R$ 500 thousand in electoral donations on the Quero Apoiar platform, leading the ranking among 2026 pre-candidates. His fundraising total reached R$ 593,223.50 with 10,232 supporters by the night of June 1st. Jones Manoel (Psol-PE) followed in second with R$ 340,414.91, then Marcel van Hattem (Novo-RS) and Humberto Matos (PCdoB-RS).

item.title: TSE mantém inelegibilidade de Cláudio Castro, ex-governador do Rio
item.description: The TSE upheld the ineligibility of former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro by rejecting clarification appeals against the ruling that convicted him of abuse of political and economic power, prohibited conduct, and illicit fundraising in the 2022 elections. The court found no omissions, obscurities, or contradictions in the March decision, stating the appeals sought to overturn the judgment rather than clarify it, which is incompatible with the purpose of clarification appeals.

item.title: Petistas atribuem tarifa de Trump a articulação de Flávio e Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: The leader of the Workers' Party (PT) in the Chamber of Deputies, Pedro Uczai (PT-SC), attributed the decision by Donald Trump's government to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian products to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL-SP). The statement was made in a video published on social media on Tuesday (2), alongside deputy Jandira Feghali (PCdoB-RJ).

item.title: Governo de SP deve abrir concurso para 2 mil PMs nos próximos dias
item.description: The São Paulo government will announce in the coming days a public competition to hire 2,000 new military police soldiers, with registration open from June 15 to August 21 and an initial monthly salary of R$5,400. The edict is ready for publication and should be released in the State Official Gazette this week, as part of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas’ plan to reach the end of his term with 26,000 new civil and military police officers in hiring, training, or integration process.

item.title: Caiado e Zema criticam chance de tarifas dos EUA e culpam Lula
item.description: Presidential pre-candidates Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Romeu Zema (Novo) criticized the U.S. proposal to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian imports, blaming the Lula administration’s foreign policy failures. They argued that Itamaraty has abandoned its traditional state policy in favor of ideological bias, damaging relations with the West and harming sectors like steel and furniture. Both pledged to reopen diplomatic and trade channels with the U.S. if elected to prevent retaliatory measures.

item.title: Haddad diz que bolsonaristas “estão todos de cabeça baixa”
item.description: Fernando Haddad, the PT’s pre-candidate for governor of São Paulo, stated that Bolsonarist militancy has lost strength in the streets due to controversies involving the right-wing in Brazil and the United States. He made the remark during a housing policy debate hosted by the Engineers’ Union in the state capital.

item.title: A decisão final do TSE sobre inelegibilidade de Cláudio Castro
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) upheld, by a 5-2 vote, the ineligibility of Cláudio Castro until 2030 due to irregular hirings in Ceperj and UERJ during the 2022 campaign. Despite the TSE ruling, the Supreme Federal Court (STF) will have the final say on whether the interim governor election in Rio will be direct or indirect, as Castro resigned to attempt to influence the format of the supplementary election.

item.title: TSE nega recurso e mantém Cláudio Castro inelegível até 2030
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) upheld the ineligibility of former governor Cláudio Castro (PL) until 2030, unanimously rejecting his appeal. The decision, by a vote of five to two, confirmed his conviction for abuse of political and economic power in the Ceperj case linked to the 2022 elections. Rapporteur Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva emphasized that no majority existed to annul his diploma, preventing that sanction, while maintaining the ineligibility ruling.

item.title: Leia a nota do governo Lula contra tarifas dos EUA
item.description: The Lula government issued a statement denouncing the U.S. proposal to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian products, calling it unjustified and linking its initiation to provocations by the Bolsonaro family in 2025. The statement accuses the Bolsonaros of acting as 'false patriots' by serving foreign interests against Brazil, rejects unilateral measures against the country and Pix, and states the government may use the Reciprocity Law to respond.

item.title: Disputa entre Lula e Flávio envolvendo os EUA expõe risco para o bolsonarismo, aponta estudo
item.description: A study by Instituto Democracia em Xeque reveals that the narrative dispute between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro over Donald Trump’s decisions exposes a risk for Bolsonarismo: Flávio’s association with the former U.S. president may be perceived as alignment with foreign interests contrary to Brazil’s national interests, especially if such measures generate concrete costs for the country. While the far-right attempted to regain political initiative by using the U.S. classification of criminal factions as terrorist to center the debate on public security, the left leveraged the moment to amplify visibility of Lula’s social deliveries and the end of the 6×1 work scale. New U.S. commercial pressures, including tariffs and scrutiny of Pix, add uncertainty to the scenario.

item.title: EUA recorrem de decisão do tribunal de comércio que determina amplos reembolsos de tarifas sob a lei de emergência
item.description: The Trump administration formally appealed a court ruling requiring customs authorities to refund $166 billion in tariffs deemed illegal by the Supreme Court, arguing the judge lacks authority to order refunds for importers who did not file lawsuits. The Department of Justice also appealed an order compelling CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott to appear in person for a hearing, while the agency reports having already returned approximately $85 billion via an online claims portal following the Supreme Court's February ruling.

item.title: TSE mantém inelegibilidade de Castro sem cassar diploma
item.description: The TSE upheld the ineligibility of former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro over abuse of power allegations in the 2022 elections, involving temporary hires by Ceperj and UERJ allegedly used as campaign operatives. The court denied the Electoral Public Ministry's request to annul his diploma, as Castro resigned on March 23, 2026, one day before the ruling was finalized.

item.title: Em carta, Flávio pede a Rubio para EUA poupar Brasil de novo tarifaço
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) sent a letter to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the exclusion of Brazil from new 25% tariffs recommended by the USTR. He argues Brazil faces severe fiscal and economic deterioration, and that tariffs would worsen the crisis, harming workers and businesses. Flávio also stated he believes he will be elected president in 2026 and offered his transition team to negotiate a broad trade and investment agreement with the United States.

item.title: Como Lula pode se beneficiar na disputa eleitoral após ‘tiro no pé’ de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Editor Robson Bonin argues that new U.S.-Brazil trade tensions could benefit Lula by allowing the government to link tariff impacts to the Bolsonaro family while avoiding direct confrontation with Trump. Flávio Bolsonaro’s U.S. visit is seen as a 'self-inflicted wound' that makes it hard for him to distance himself politically, strengthening Lula’s narrative on national sovereignty.

item.title: Governo do Distrito Federal contratou por R$ 5 milhões ONG ligada a produtora de 'Dark Horse'
item.description: The Federal District government contracted the NGO Instituto Conhecer Brasil for R$ 5 million to implement the Steam Maker program in 16 schools, funding robotics kits, 3D printers, and computers. The contract, initially R$ 4 million, was increased by R$ 1 million and extended to December 2025. Meanwhile, São Paulo’s Civil Police are investigating whether public funds transferred to the same NGO by the city hall were diverted to finance the production of the film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro, involving the production company Go Up Entertainment and allies of federal deputy Mário Frias.

item.title: Leia a carta de Flávio a Rubio pedindo que EUA poupem Brasil de tarifas
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) sent a letter to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the exclusion of Brazil from a proposed 25% tariff on certain imports by the USTR. He warned that Brazil faces 'serious fiscal and economic deterioration', with rising public debt and record delinquency, and that tariffs would worsen the crisis. The letter followed his White House visit, where he was photographed with Donald Trump and Eduardo Bolsonaro, and included praise for the U.S. designation of Brazilian criminal gangs as terrorist organizations.

item.title: TSE confirma condenação de Cláudio Castro
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously upheld the conviction of former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro for irregularities in the 2022 electoral process. The ruling keeps him ineligible for office until 2030 and sparks debate over who should choose his successor — the electorate or political parties.

item.title: Kassio Nunes Marques conhece iniciativas do TRE-PR voltadas à inclusão indígena e à modernização da Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, president of the TSE, made his first official visit to a regional electoral court at the TRE-PR, where he learned about the Indigenous Peoples’ Ombuds Office and other inclusion and modernization initiatives. He emphasized the importance of the specialized ombuds office in ensuring effective access to political rights for Indigenous peoples, stating that the TRE-PR model will be replicated in other regional courts. Activists and experts praised the initiatives as key to increasing Indigenous participation as voters, election workers, and candidates.

item.title: TSE mantém condenação de Castro. Definição sobre eleição no RJ deve ficar para o STF
item.description: The TSE upheld Cláudio Castro's conviction for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections, maintaining his ineligibility until 2030. While rejecting the MPE's request for diploma cassation, it partially accepted Castro's appeal to correct a material error in the fine. The final decision on supplementary elections in Rio de Janeiro will be made by the STF, which has the case under review after a view request by Minister Flávio Dino.

item.title: Bastidores: por telefone, Lula aprovou nota do governo contra tarifaço de Trump. Ministros vão buscar EUA para negociação
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva approved, by phone, a government statement in response to the U.S. threat to impose 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods. The approval came during an emergency meeting of the government’s top leadership, which will determine next diplomatic steps, including sending ministers to the U.S. for negotiations.

item.title: Lula responsabiliza clã Bolsonaro por ataque dos EUA ao Pix e taxação
item.description: President Lula accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of asking U.S. President Donald Trump to interfere with Brazil's Pix payment system during a White House meeting. Lula claimed the alleged request led the U.S. to propose a 25% tax on Brazilian products, threatening 21% of Brazil's exports to the U.S., and criticized Bolsonaro for now denying the request, saying it harms the Brazilian people and agribusiness.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro se encontra com Eduardo Cunha em BH
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and pre-candidate for president in 2026, met with former deputy Eduardo Cunha in Belo Horizonte on Tuesday (2). During the meeting, Flávio gave an interview to a radio station linked to Cunha and spoke about tax burden, entrepreneurship, and social programs. Cunha, who was removed from office and arrested in Operation Lava Jato and announced his candidacy for federal deputy from MG in 2026, stated that Flávio has taken on the mission of leading the conservative field in the 2026 election.

item.title: Diretor-geral da PF defende novo inquérito para investigar recursos de Vorcaro para ‘Dark Horse’
item.description: Federal Police Director-General Andrei Rodrigues advocated for a new investigation into Daniel Vorcaro's transfer of funds to the U.S. under the guise of financing the film 'Dark Horse', proposing three procedural paths: merging with the 'Master case' (STF, rapporteur Justice André Mendonça), incorporating into the existing inquiry on Eduardo Bolsonaro's U.S. activities (Justice Alexandre de Moraes), or random assignment to another STF justice. Rodrigues also denounced the classification of PCC and CV as terrorist groups as a 'technical error' that undermines effective crime-fighting.

item.title: TSE rejeita recursos e mantém Cláudio Castro inelegível
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously upheld the ineligibility of former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) for abuse of political and economic power in a scheme involving the irregular hiring of tens of thousands of campaign workers. While the court corrected the legal basis of the fine imposed, it rejected the Electoral Public Ministry’s request to formally annul Castro’s and ex-vice-governor Thiago Pampolha’s diplomas, maintaining that the mandate’s cancellation was moot due to their resignation one day before the ruling.

item.title: TSE rejeita recurso da defesa e mantém condenação de Cláudio Castro
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously upheld the conviction of former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections, rendering him ineligible until 2030. While the Court rejected the Electoral Prosecution’s request to formally annul his diploma, a disagreement remains over whether his resignation nullifies the cassation, with direct implications for whether the state will hold direct or indirect elections to fill the vacancy.

item.title: Bolsonaristas estão 'de cabeça baixa' com Trump e caso Master, diz Haddad
item.description: Fernando Haddad said Bolsonarist militants are 'head down' due to U.S. sanctions and investigations into Banco Master and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. He noted that while Bolsonarist presence has faded in public spaces, it remains strong online, and linked Governor Tarcísio de Freitas to Bolsonarism and the far right. Haddad also criticized the privatization of Sabesp and called for a 'union and reconstruction' plan for São Paulo, speaking at a housing policy debate.

item.title: Tarifa dos EUA ameaça 21% das exportações e governo busca acordo
item.description: The U.S. government recommended a 25% additional tariff on part of Brazilian exports, which could affect 21% of Brazil's total sales to the U.S. The Lula administration said it will continue negotiating to avoid the measure, emphasizing that issues like Pix, financial sovereignty, and environmental policies are non-negotiable. Talks continue until July 15, with a new meeting scheduled in Paris during an OECD event.

item.title: Auditoria interna da Cedae aponta prejuízo de R$ 220 milhões com Master e roteiro semelhante ao do Rioprevidência
item.description: An internal audit by Cedae found the company may have lost over R$ 220 million in investments at Banco Master after the finance department ignored internal warnings about the bank’s deteriorating condition. The report reveals that investment rules were relaxed in September 2023 to match Banco Master’s profile, which had initially been deemed ineligible due to its substandard risk rating and single-agency evaluation. The investigation suggests possible negligence, systemic misconduct, fraud, and asset risk, implicating former finance director Antonio Carlos dos Santos.
